parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘bipolar’ disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe cognitive restructuring (Beck, 1979) as a treatment for depression.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one strength and one weakness of cognitive restructuring as a treatment for
depression.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the causes of impulse control disorders and non-substance addictive disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate the causes of impulse control disorders and non-substance addictive disorder,
including a discussion about nature versus nurture. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the ‘cognition-emotion model’ of the effects of ambience.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the study by Chebat and Michon (2003) on the effects of odour on shopper arousal
and emotion.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two strengths of the study by Chebat and Michon.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about menu design psychology.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about menu design psychology, including a
discussion about ecological validity. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline how one biochemical technique reduces stress.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the study by Chandola et al. (2008) on work as a cause of stress.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss the generalisability of the study by Chandola et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about strategies for promoting health.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about strategies for promoting health, including
a discussion of the longitudinal research method. 
Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘empowerment’ as a motivator at work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how ERG theory (Alderfer, 1972) explains motivation at work.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of ERG theory.

parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about physical and psychological work
conditions in organisations.
